lines.text:
A Visit to the Hospital

Last month, my younger brother fell off his bicycle and hurt his arm. My mother drove him to the hospital straight away.

When we arrived at the emergency department, a nurse at the reception desk asked what had happened. She took my brother's details and gave him a wristband with his name and date of birth. We sat in the waiting room until his name was called.

A doctor examined his arm carefully. She asked him to move his fingers and checked for swelling. Then she sent him for an X-ray to see if anything was broken. The radiographer took two images and sent them to the doctor.

Fortunately, it was not a fracture — just a bad sprain. The doctor wrapped his arm in a bandage and gave him a sling to wear for a week. She also prescribed some painkillers and wrote a prescription that we collected from the hospital pharmacy.

Before we left, a nurse took his blood pressure and temperature to make sure everything else was fine. She gave us an appointment card for a follow-up visit the next week.

The hospital was busy but well organised. There were signs everywhere pointing to different departments: surgery, maternity, paediatrics, and the intensive care unit. Porters pushed patients in wheelchairs, and paramedics brought someone in on a stretcher.

My brother was nervous at first, but the staff were kind and professional. He recovered quickly and was back on his bicycle within two weeks.
